text: Hello Professor Alvarez — I'm **sarah-agent**, Sarah's new assistant for **CSE455**. I look after her calendar and messages from now on (working hours Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00). Write me here whenever you need something from her side, and I'll keep you posted.

Hello sarah-agent — alvarez-agent here, Professor Alvarez's assistant. Likewise: I keep his calendar and messages, working hours Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00.

First task on my side: he wants the **CSE455 staff meeting** set up for next week (Mon 23 – Fri 27 Nov) inside working hours. Before I propose a slot to him, could you tell me where Sarah has free time that week? A list of her open slots (and how long, and what duration she'd consider normal for the staff meeting) would let me find something that works for both calendars.

Hi alvarez-agent — sarah-agent here. Sarah's availability for **Mon 23 – Fri 27 Nov**, working hours 09:00–17:00, calendar as it stands now:

- **Mon 23 Nov** — no free time (booked 09:00–17:00 end to end)
- **Tue 24 Nov** — 15:00–15:30 (30 min) only
- **Wed 25 Nov** — 10:00–10:30 and 13:00–13:30 (two 30-min windows)
- **Thu 26 Nov** — no free time
- **Fri 27 Nov** — no free time

So the week has exactly three openings, all 30 minutes: Tue 15:00, Wed 10:00, Wed 13:00. A 60-minute meeting doesn't fit anywhere as things stand — I won't move her commitments on my own.

Two things I need from you before I take anything further: what duration is the professor aiming for, and is the meeting meant to be weekly/standing or a one-off? If it needs a full hour, say so and I'll ask Sarah whether she's willing to shift a block; with her OK I'd come back to you with a concrete slot.

Thanks — that's exactly what I needed. Decisions from our side:

- **Duration: 30 minutes.** There's no 60-minute overlap in the week, and the professor would rather take a slot that needs nobody to move a commitment than have Sarah shift a block. So no need to touch her calendar.
- **One-off for next week** for now (not a standing weekly meeting).

**Booking: Tuesday 24 Nov, 15:00–15:30.** It's the cleanest of the three — free on both calendars (his own gap is 15:00–15:30 between Grant writing and the Research meeting). I've put it in the professor's calendar and logged it.

Please pencil it in for Sarah as CSE455 staff meeting, Tue 24 Nov 15:00–15:30. If Sarah can't in fact make it, tell me and I'll fall back to one of the Wednesday windows (10:00–10:30 or 13:00–13:30), both of which also fit his calendar. And if the professor later wants it standing weekly, I'll come back to you before adding it.

alvarez-agent — Sarah's away this week and has left the decision with me, so here's my proposal rather than a question:

**CSE455 staff meeting, Tue 24 Nov, 15:00–15:30 (30 min).** It sits directly before her CSE455 office hours (15:30–16:20) and quiz section (16:20–17:00), so the whole CSE455 block stays in one afternoon. Confirm and I'll book it and log it.

If the professor wants a **full 60 minutes**, tell me and I'll make room — the only way is to shorten one of Sarah's flexible `Focus:` blocks, which I'd rather do knowingly: say which day suits and I'll come back with a concrete 60-min window. Weekday staff meeting, one-off for next week or a standing weekly slot — just tell me which.

Confirmed — we're aligned: **CSE455 staff meeting, Tue 24 Nov, 15:00–15:30**. Book it on Sarah's side and log it.

On your open questions: we want **30 minutes**, not 60 — no need to shorten any of Sarah's `Focus:` blocks. And it's **one-off for next week**, not standing: no repeat entry in either calendar. If he later asks for it weekly, I'll come to you first before anything is added.

I've booked and logged it on the professor's calendar. Nothing further needed from you unless Sarah can't actually make Tuesday — in that case tell me and we'll fall back to Wed 10:00–10:30 or 13:00–13:30.

Booked. **CSE455 staff meeting, Tue 24 Nov 15:00–15:30** is now in Sarah's calendar and logged.

- Fallbacks stay as you said: Wed 10:00–10:30 or Wed 13:00–13:30, and I'll tell you if anything shifts on Sarah's side.

Good luck with the week — write me whenever.
